title: Which data management tool fits you?

questions.q: What is the pain you have today?
questions.hint: The post says to start from the pain, because no single tool does every job.

options.label: I cannot get the data from our apps and databases
Reports are slow or the data sits in too many places
options.why: you need a place to store and query data

options.label: Nobody knows which table is right or who owns it
The numbers broke and we heard it from a customer
Sales and finance have different customer lists
A vendor runs it for me
options.why: you want the vendor to run it

options.label: Either, I want a managed option and a self-run option
options.why: it offers a vendor-run route and a self-run route

questions.q: What does your budget look like?

options.label: Free software, we will pay in servers and people
options.why: it is free, Apache-2.0 or free to run yourself

options.label: A free tier or published price I can check
options.why: it has a free plan or a price you can read

options.label: A quote and a contract are fine
options.why: its price comes from a quote

questions.q: Where does your data have to live?

options.label: On Google Cloud
options.why: you are already on Google Cloud

options.label: On Microsoft
options.why: Microsoft is already your home base

options.label: Everything must run in our own environment
options.why: you can run it in your own environment

questions.q: What skills does your team have?

options.label: Engineers who write Python
options.why: your engineers can write the rules and code

options.label: Platform engineers who run services
options.why: you can run services on Kubernetes

options.label: Few engineers
options.why: you want a vendor to carry the work

fivetran.name: Fivetran
fivetran.summary: A managed service that moves your data using ready-made connectors.
fivetran.bestWhen: You want a managed pipeline service and can accept per-row billing.
fivetran.watchOut: Paid per-row rates sit in a separate table, so your bill depends on your row counts and connections.

airbyte.name: Airbyte
airbyte.summary: Open-source connectors you can self-host, or pay for as Cloud.
airbyte.bestWhen: You have engineers and want control or a lower starting price.
airbyte.watchOut: Its CDC docs say syncs are scheduled and that CDC incremental needs primary keys for most sources, and Core uses the ELv2 licence, which restricts resale as a hosted service.

olake.name: OLake Go
olake.summary: Open-source replication of Postgres, MySQL/MariaDB, MongoDB and SQL Server (plus Oracle, Db2, S3 and Kafka sources) into Iceberg or Parquet.
olake.bestWhen: Your data sits in databases and you want Iceberg or Parquet on storage you run.
olake.watchOut: It moves data, so catalog, quality and master data are other tools' jobs.

bigquery.name: Google BigQuery
bigquery.summary: A serverless warehouse billed per TiB scanned, with the first 1 TiB of queries a month free.
bigquery.bestWhen: You are on Google Cloud and want pay-per-query.
bigquery.watchOut: It is a Google Cloud service with no self-hosted option stated, and busy projects share query capacity.

purview.name: Microsoft Purview
purview.summary: A catalog and governance product that sits next to security and compliance tools.
purview.bestWhen: Microsoft is already your home base.
purview.watchOut: Billing is per governed asset, and its Learn page lists Data Security Posture Management as in preview.

openmetadata.name: OpenMetadata
openmetadata.summary: A free, Apache-2.0 catalog with quality checks and governance workflows.
openmetadata.bestWhen: You have platform engineers and want no licence fee.
openmetadata.watchOut: You run it yourself for production, on Kubernetes, cloud services or bare metal, unless you buy a managed version.

datahub.name: DataHub
datahub.summary: An Apache-2.0 catalog you can self-host, with a managed DataHub Cloud route.
datahub.bestWhen: You want open source now and a managed option later.
datahub.watchOut: We found no DataHub Cloud price, and self-hosting means running it yourself, with Docker or Helm charts.

greatexpectations.name: Great Expectations
greatexpectations.summary: A free Python library that checks your data against rules you write.
greatexpectations.watchOut: It is a Python library for data validation, so you write the rules and run them in code.

informatica.name: Informatica
informatica.summary: A large vendor with master data, catalog, integration and quality products.
informatica.bestWhen: You want a single large vendor and a negotiated contract.
informatica.watchOut: No dollar price per unit appears on its pricing page, so you need a quote.

snowflake.name: Snowflake
snowflake.summary: A fully managed cloud data platform with consumption-based pricing.
snowflake.watchOut: Dollar rates sit in a separate table, and no self-hosted option is stated.

databricks.name: Databricks
databricks.summary: A data and AI platform on AWS, Azure and Google Cloud, billed pay as you go.
databricks.bestWhen: Your team writes code and trains models.
databricks.watchOut: Managed Iceberg tables need Unity Catalog and serverless compute, and billing is pay as you go.

collibra.name: Collibra
collibra.summary: A governance product with shared business terms, named owners, policy checks and automated stewardship workflows.
collibra.bestWhen: You have a governance team and room for a demo cycle.
collibra.watchOut: No price is published, so you need to ask for a quote.

semarchy.name: Semarchy xDM
semarchy.summary: A focused master data tool offered as SaaS or on-premises.
semarchy.bestWhen: Master data is your main problem.
semarchy.watchOut: No price is published, so you need to ask for a quote.
